newsitem.title: USA: A.M. Best downgrades PCA Property & Casualty.
newsitem.headline: A.M. Best downgrades PCA Property & Casualty.

text.p: Insurance rating agency A.M. Best Co said it downgraded PCA Property & Casualty Insurance Co to "E" (under state supervision) following the insurer's $48 million shortfall in its third quarter results.
The Florida Department of Insurance placed the Altamonte Springs, Fla.-based company under administrative supervision, A.M. Best said.
A.M. Best said the Florida agency mandated an actuarial study that led to a $150 million charge against third quarter earnings, representing reserve strengthening.
Upon further review, the company posted an additional loss-reserve charge of $80 million in the fourth quarter, A.M. Best said.
The company had projected a deficit of $128 million at the end of 1996, A.M. Best said.
A court hearing about PCA Property & Casualty is set for May 2, 1997, about whether the company should be taken into rehabilitation by the state, A.M. Best said.

A circuit court judge has prohibited PCA Property & Casualty and its officers from removing any assets or records from the company, A.M. Best said. PCA Property & Casualty has been ordered to stop writing new and renewal workers compensation and other lines of business, A.M. Best said.
An automatic stay was granted that prevents others from initiating judicial or other proceedings against PCA Property & Casualty's assets, A.M. Best said.
